mechanism_narrative: The EGFR-IL6ST novokine with a rigid_helix_40 linker (~60 Å) forces an RTK (EGFR, 1210 aa, ECD ~621 aa) into proximity with a cytokine receptor (IL6ST/gp130, 918 aa, ECD ~597 aa). EGFR's intrinsic tyrosine kinase transphosphorylates IL6ST's cytoplasmic tyrosines, creating docking sites for GRB2-SHC1 (MAPK), GAB1-PIK3R1 (PI3K/AKT), and STAT3 (JAK-STAT). Simultaneously, IL6ST-associated JAK1/JAK2 phosphorylate EGFR tyrosines, amplifying GRB2 and STAT3 recruitment. PLCG1 is sterically excluded because its SH2 domain requires specific phosphotyrosine spacing that the asymmetric RTK-cytokine geometry cannot provide. FRS2/FRS3 are also excluded as they are FGFR-specific adaptors. The biased output is synergistic MAPK + PI3K/AKT + STAT3 activation, promoting a muscle structural gene program (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN) enriched in young muscle while suppressing aged IEGs (EGR1, FOS, JUN) and inflammatory/senescence markers (IL32, TXNIP, CDKN2A).
